newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq condemns Turkey over U.S.-led air patrols.
newsitem.headline: Iraq condemns Turkey over U.S.-led air patrols.

text.p: Iraq condemned on Friday a Turkish decision to extend a U.S.-led aerial surveillance operation in northern Iraq, saying Ankara was implementing a "harmful" policy against Baghdad.

A statement by an Iraqi foreign ministry spokesman also warned that the extension, approved by Turkish MPs on Thursday, and a Turkish security operation in northern Iraq would damage Turkey's interests.

"Iraq strongly condemns the Turkish parliament's decision to renew for another six months the presence of American and British aggressive forces on its territory in order to continue their aggression against Iraq," the statement carried by the official Iraqi News Agency INA said.
The U.S.-British Northern Watch planes have been patrolling the skies of northern Iraq to protect Kurds from any attack by Baghdad since the Gulf War ended in 1991.
The operation, previously named Provide Comfort, was redubbed Northern Watch following the withdrawal of French aircrafts at the end of last year.
"Iraq holds Turkey fully responsible for its harmful policies against Iraq which confirm Turkey's ignorance of good neighbourly relations and of international law and the United Nations charter."

"The continuing Turkish military invasion of northern Iraq and Turkish parliament's extension of American and British troops on Turkish territory to commit aggression on Iraq...would threaten Turkey's real interests," the statement said without elaborating.
Turkish security forces, involved in a six-week campaign against Kurdish rebels in northern Iraq, have now mostly withdrawn from the region.
Iraq and Turkey had concluded several trade deals, the last of which was signed in May to set up a gas pipeline to supply Turkey with 10 billion cubic metres of gas a year.
Iraq has been purchasing Turkish goods under an oil-for-food deal signed with the United Nations.
"Such a double standard policy (by Turkey) would yield nothing but harm to Turkish interests and an attempt to drain Iraq and Turkey's energies," the spokesman said.
